rounds: Frightening adverts do more good than funny ones.
Most people already know what’s good for them; they just don’t do it.
Posters and adverts hardly ever change anyone’s habits.
Health warnings on wine and beer should be as big as on cigarettes.
Speed cameras should be hidden, not painted in bright colours.
A sugar tax would do more good than any healthy-eating campaign.
The state has no business telling adults how much to drink.
Safety campaigns should aim at children, because adults never change.
